audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings claim Steadfast Presence denies or nullifies Nasus's commit: mid "her W Steadfast Presence can negate your committed step-up", late "her W denies your dash-less all-in", spikes[3].text "Steadfast Presence W will deny your dash-less commit", wants.foe[1] "nullify any committed step-up", whys[5] "her W Steadfast Presence can still deny a committed all-in".
audit.why: Steadfast Presence's active stops enemy DASHES around her, and grounds and slows whatever it stopped. Nasus has no dash anywhere in his kit — he walks in, which is exactly why the text keeps saying "dash-less" in the same breath as claiming the ability denies him. Against this specific champion Poppy's signature anti-engage button does nothing but give her move speed. Telling a Nasus to hold his all-in for a W that cannot touch him gives away his only good window in the lane, every time.
audit.corrected: Steadfast Presence's active cannot stop you — you have no dash. What still matters is its passive armour and MR, which climb as her health drops.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings give Hammer Shock a knockup — early "her Q knockup out-trades anything you throw", spikes[0].text "Q knockup", whys[0] "Q knockup", wants.foe[0] "a free Q knockup".
audit.why: Hammer Shock has no knockup. It deals damage and leaves a zone that slows and then explodes after a delay, on a 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown at 430 range. The only knockup in Poppy's kit is Keeper's Verdict (R). Expecting to be knocked up by her Q means misreading every trade she opens.
audit.corrected: Hammer Shock is a damage-plus-slow zone that detonates after a delay. The knockup is her ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Keeper's Verdict is never mentioned in either layer, and neither is her passive Iron Ambassador.
audit.why: Keeper's Verdict is a 140/120/100s channelled knockup that throws enemies very far and makes Poppy untargetable while she charges it. For a Nasus whose entire late game is walking at people in a side lane, being hammered out of the fight is the single cleanest way she beats him after laning — and the matchup text has nothing on it at all. Iron Ambassador gives her a free shield when she picks the buckler back up, which is small but real in the short trades the early section describes.
audit.corrected: Name Keeper's Verdict as the tool that removes you from a fight you were winning.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers.
audit.why: There is some sequencing already ("Bait her E first", "Save Wither for after she burns E") but never a number, so the player has no idea how long the window lasts. Heroic Charge is 14/13/12/11/10s at 475 range — a missed pin at rank 1 leaves her without her only escape or engage for fourteen seconds, which is the whole basis for the bait advice the text already gives.
audit.corrected: Attach the 14s figure to the existing bait-the-E instruction.

edits.before: Poppy owns these levels and you cannot contest it. Her W passively gives her bonus armor and shrugs damage, her Q knockup out-trades anything you throw, and her E will pin you to a wall for a stun the second you walk up. Do not try to trade for stacks — last-hit with Siphoning Strike from max range, sit near your tower, and never stand with the river or tower wall behind you or her E becomes a free combo. Use Spirit Fire to safely farm and chip her if she dives the wave.
edits.after: Poppy owns these levels and you cannot contest it. Steadfast Presence passively gives her armor and MR that grow as she drops low, Hammer Shock (Q) lays a slow zone that detonates after a delay, and Heroic Charge (E) will pin you to a wall for a stun the second you walk up. Do not trade for stacks — last-hit with Siphoning Strike from max range and never stand with the river or tower wall behind you. Use Spirit Fire to farm safely and chip her off the wave.

edits.before: Level 6 is your one window. Fury of the Sands plus Wither lets you slow her movement and attack speed to nothing and grind her down with lifesteal before she can reset the fight. Bait her E first — if she misses the wall-pin or burns it on the wave, that is when you ult and Wither and run her over. But respect that her W Steadfast Presence can negate your committed step-up, so only all-in when Wither is up and she has no wall behind you to throw you into.
edits.after: Level 6 is your one window. Fury of the Sands plus Wither slows her movement and attack speed to nothing and grinds her down with lifesteal. Bait Heroic Charge first — it is 14s at rank 1, so a missed pin hands you that whole window to ult, Wither and run her over. Her W active only stops dashes and you have none, so it will not deny your step-up at all; what it does give her is move speed and resists that climb as she falls.

edits.before: Once you have real stacks and items the lane finally tips your way — your empowered Q and Soul Eater lifesteal out-grind her even trades, and Wither shuts her down in any extended duel. She is not a hard scaler so she does not reclaim the late game the way Vayne or Fiora would. The catch stays her toolkit: her W denies your dash-less all-in and her E can still pin you mid-fight, so fight with Wither and ult available and never commit next to a wall.

notes: The Steadfast-Presence error is the interesting one: the text repeatedly writes "your dash-less all-in" while asserting that a dash-stopping ability denies it, so the contradiction was sitting in the same sentence. Poppy W being blank against Nasus is a genuine edge in a matchup the data has Nasus losing at 48.11%, and it is exactly the sort of thing an auto-generated page will never surface. The packet's suspectName "Use Spirit Fire" in early is a false positive — Nasus's own E, correctly named. I did not write anything off Hammer Shock's `grounding` kit flag; Riot's text for that ability describes only damage, a slow zone and a delayed explosion, so I treat the flag as unverified.
